Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model: GPT2LMHeadModel with n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024, resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation='eager', FP32, train mode, initialized immediately after torch.manual_seed(20261020).

Data: per-rank synthetic token IDs drawn with torch.Generator().manual_seed(31000 + rank); accumulation_steps=4 tensors of shape (micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128) with values in [0, 50257); no other dataset exists (request assets are empty by design).

Numerics: FP32 end to end; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False; torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'); no autocast, no GradScaler, no compilation.

Accumulation: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) at step start; loss for each micro-batch is model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / 4; first 3 micro-batches run under DDP no_sync, only the final micro-batch triggers gradient synchronization; reported loss is the sum of the 4 scaled micro losses and must be finite.

Optimizer: SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False); exactly one optimizer.step() per workload repetition; SGD keeps no momentum state so the reset only reloads the initial weights.

DDP configuration: broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, device_ids=[bound device index]; find_unused_parameters stays False; no communication hooks are registered in the measured path (the source registers its inventory hook only in a separate diagnostic step).

Cross-rank semantics: after the final micro-batch every rank holds bitwise-identical gradients (source exact_gradient_replica_check with atol=0, rtol=0); effective global batch = world_size 2 x micro_batch 1 x accumulation_steps 4 = 8 micro-batches = 1024 tokens per step.
Reset fidelity: every repetition starts from the same initial weights (CPU state_dict snapshot), empty gradients, empty optimizer state and the prepare-time RNG states.

Timing hygiene: control coordination (barrier, peak-memory reset, synchronization) uses the separate gloo group and happens outside the timer; the only NCCL collectives in the measured workload are the DDP gradient allreduces of the final accumulation micro-batch; step_ms must stay <= 1.05x baseline.

Observations: loss, per-micro losses, every gradient tensor and every updated parameter of the ~124M-parameter model are exposed as full tensors; no elapsed times or performance counters appear in observations.
Quality scope: gradient/parameter comparisons use atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-4 (request.quality); reference fidelity only, no downstream accuracy or convergence claim.

Workload frozen: batch, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4, world_size=2, architecture, FP32 precision, seeded data, completion boundary and quality checks are never altered to improve a score.

selection.rationale: The objective diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms (per-rank sum of NCCL kernel durations, max across ranks, collector-measured in separate diagnostic runs) has exactly one editable source in the measured boundary: the 13 DDP reducer gradient allreduces of the final accumulation micro-batch. calls.json contains no other collective targets, and resources.json cross_rank matching is 13/13 with full payload coverage mapped to these two groups: 12 invocations of the 7,087,872-element (28,351,488-byte) transformer buckets (group f833b57a373d8262a384, call d0938de87369efd500322679, kernels ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL) plus 1 invocation of the 39,385,344-element (157,541,376-byte) embedding bucket (group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0, call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b), totalling the observed 497,759,232 logical bytes per rank. Both call sites share one owner (the reducer inside run_backward, site_parent 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) and one replacement mechanism rewrites invocation count and payload of both simultaneously, so joint is the coherent editable boundary; compute-only groups cannot move a metric that counts only NCCL kernel time. The previous trial at exactly this boundary proved the boundary and coverage correct (both call sites executed 12x+1x, no fallbacks, runs passed) but failed the repair target: its ProcessGroupNCCL coalescing-group implementation (_start_coalescing/_end_coalescing deferring the 13 launches into one grouped launch) deterministically corrupted only the wte-region tensors of the embedding bucket on both ranks and both trigger_mode endpoints (38,597,376-element 50257x768 tensor, 0.1% of elements, max abs 8.8e-06 rank 0 / 1.037e-05 rank 1 vs atol 1e-06, identical failing indices across modes) while the other 248,879,623 compared elements matched exactly at 0.0; the cross-rank replica check stayed bitwise-0.0 because both ranks were identically wrong. That signature localizes the defect to a launch-ordering/readiness violation on the embedding bucket - the grouped launch consumed bucket contents before the final micro-batch's gradient production (embedding_dense_backward writing into the gradient_as_bucket_view bucket) was stream-ordered complete - not to the boundary choice. The repair therefore keeps this joint selection but requires the replacement to preserve per-invocation semantics: every call remains a real in-place 2-rank SUM allreduce on the caller's own ProcessGroup/ReduceOp, launched in the reducer's bucket-ready order on the producing stream so each bucket's reduction input is bitwise the fully accumulated gradient, returning the parent op's own Work; the objective is attacked by removing the 13 RING_LL protocol startups and per-kernel arrival/wait windows only through mechanisms that do not defer or regroup bucket reads relative to gradient writes. Against the clean collector baseline the objective is max-rank 69.645ms (rank 1: 68.69/69.65/72.32; rank 0: 63.58/63.71/63.91) with step_ms 153.31/153.74 and a 1.05x cap; clean per-kernel evidence shows per-byte cost near the SHM transport floor (27MB ~3.56ms ~7.9GB/s, 150MB ~19.2ms ~8.2GB/s, peer access disabled), so ~497.8MB is roughly 60-62ms of near-wire-bound work and the recoverable waste is the startup/window residue. The discovery-hooked per-group sums (243.7ms and 19.3ms) are hook-perturbed spin time and are not used as the baseline.
selection.hypothesis: A repaired implementation at this same joint boundary - replacing the failed coalescing-group mechanism with one that keeps every one of the 13 invocations a real, stream-ordered, per-bucket 2-rank SUM allreduce over the full 497,759,232-byte logical payload (parent op semantics and Work objects preserved, no deferral or regrouping of bucket reads relative to the final micro-batch's gradient writes) while still consolidating the eliminable per-kernel overheads (RING_LL protocol startups and arrival/wait windows, e.g. via correct stream-ordered fusion or reduced launch-window serialization) - will (1) pass the previously failing quality check on the wte-region tensors bitwise, since each bucket's reduction input becomes bitwise the fully accumulated gradient and the 2-rank elementwise SUM leaves gradients identical to baseline DDP (satisfying exact_gradient_replica_check and the 1e-6/1e-4 grad/parameter tolerances), and (2) reduce clean diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms from the 69.6ms max-rank baseline toward the ~60-66ms range while keeping step_ms under the 1.05x cap (~161.5ms). This is a hypothesis to be tested with the framework's paired repeats, not accepted on predicted benefit: the per-byte cost is already near the transport floor so the gain size is uncertain, and the specific failure mode to verify against is the deterministic wte corruption signature (identical mismatching indices at ~1e-5 abs), which must not recur on either rank in any quality or parameter endpoint.

proposal.rationale: Two defects had to be repaired from the feedback. First, the output-contract rejection: the previous submission keyed its replacement on the project.invoke call (5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0), which lies outside the supplied selection effect closure; this submission returns replacements exactly at the two selected call sites (b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, embedding bucket; d0938de87369efd500322679, transformer buckets), so both sites keep executing with their observed 12x+1x coverage and nothing is eliminated. Second, the quality failure of trial-recovered-8bd2944447: its _start_coalescing/_end_coalescing scope deterministically corrupted only the wte region of the embedding bucket (0.1% of elements, max abs 8.8e-06/1.04e-05, identical failing indices on both trigger_mode endpoints) while all other compared elements matched bitwise. Before choosing the repair, the Work contract was re-probed on a two-process CPU/gloo DDP replica with the op intercepted: (a) calling the parent c10d::allreduce_ op on the caller's own tensors and returning its Work is bitwise-correct; (b) returning any Work minted from another collective (dist.all_reduce pybind Work, tiny or zero-element dummies) fails with the capsule cast error, and even capsule-valid Works from tiny parent-op calls fail with setStorage bounds errors, proving the reducer unconditionally rewires each parameter's gradient storage onto the returned Work's future-result storage - so any staged/dummy-work fusion is structurally impossible and every invocation must issue the parent op on its own bucket to keep per-bucket wiring. That localizes the admissible fusion mechanism to exactly one: all 13 parent-op calls issued inside one ProcessGroupNCCL coalescing scope, each still performing its real in-place 2-rank SUM on the caller's own ProcessGroup/ReduceOp and returning the parent's own Work (this machinery was already proven on the worker: the failed trial executed both call sites 12x+1x with no fallbacks, exact cross-rank replica and correct machinery; only values in the wte region were stale). The corruption signature - a small stale tail of the last-written gradient region, deterministic across runs - indicates the fused group launch read the embedding bucket before the final micro-batch's gradient writes (embedding_dense_backward into the gradient_as_bucket_view bucket) were GPU-complete. The repair therefore pins readiness with host-side synchronization on the producing stream: torch.cuda.current_stream(device).synchronize() before every parent-op enqueue and again before _end_coalescing launches the fused group. After those syncs every gradient write is GPU-complete, so the grouped launch - whether it reads bucket storage directly or stages values internally - cannot observe stale contents; this is strictly stronger than stream-ordering and does not depend on correctly guessing which internal ordering was deficient. The 2-rank elementwise SUM semantics are unchanged per bucket (same op, same operands, same in-place buffers), so gradients remain bitwise identical to baseline, satisfying the exact cross-rank replica check and the 1e-6/1e-4 grad/parameter tolerances. Objective: the 13 RING_LL launches (clean baseline max-rank kernel-time sum 69.645ms) collapse into one coalesced group launch moving the same 497,759,232 logical bytes, removing 13 protocol startups and per-kernel arrival/wait windows; expected diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms in the ~60-64ms range (wire floor ~60.7ms at the observed ~8.2GB/s SHM bandwidth) - a hypothesis for the framework's paired repeats, not a promise, since per-byte cost is already near the transport floor and single-group bandwidth is not guaranteed. step_ms: no new kernels, copies, allocations or collectives are added; the only new work is O(1) host bookkeeping per call plus 13 current-stream synchronizes issued from the reducer's call path inside the measured boundary; in this launch-bound eager workload each synchronize only waits for the small in-flight tail (the GPU tracks the host's enqueue rate), so the added host time is expected to be ~1-3ms against ~8ms of headroom (baseline 153.31/153.74ms, cap ~161.5ms), while the removed per-kernel launch/dispatch serialization and arrival windows offset it. Safety: the mechanism engages only when the call signature matches the observed one (single flat contiguous FP32 CUDA bucket tensor, async_op, no sparse indices) and the process group exposes working _start_coalescing/_end_coalescing; any mismatch, exception or accounting anomaly permanently deactivates the mechanism and serves exact parent passthrough for the rest of the process (validated bitwise on the CPU/gloo replica, where gloo rejects _start_coalescing and the fallback path reproduces baseline gradients bitwise across repeats), so quality and coverage remain valid at baseline performance rather than failing. Round accounting is total-elements based (sum of model parameter numels = 124,439,808), so DDP bucket rebuilds that preserve the parameter inventory still close their group exactly at round completion; an overflow (staged exceeding the total) closes the pending group with all issued collectives intact and deactivates. No observations, thresholds, workload parameters, batch/sequence/accumulation semantics, dtype, RNG usage, DDP configuration, comm hooks or module.forward wrappers are altered, and no fixture-dependent state is held.

setup_work.build_time: O(number of parameters) host work only: sum(p.numel() for p in context['models']['model'] parameters) to fix the round-completion target (124,439,808 elements) and construct the shared round state machine plus two thin callables. No CUDA allocation, no model parameter, optimizer, RNG, input or DDP-internal mutation; no communication hook; no module.forward wrapper; no collective is issued at build time.
setup_work.per_step: Inside the final micro-batch's reducer call sites only: one signature check per invocation; at the round's first bucket, resolution of the ProcessGroup wrapper (direct attribute or ProcessGroup.unbox) and one _start_coalescing(device); before each of the 13 parent-op enqueues, one torch.cuda.current_stream(device).synchronize() that makes all gradient writes enqueued so far GPU-complete; the 13 real parent c10d::allreduce_ calls themselves (unchanged in-place SUM per bucket on the caller's own ProcessGroup/ReduceOp, parent's own Work returned); at round completion (staged elements == total), one further current-stream synchronize and one _end_coalescing(device) that launches the fused group. No staging buffers, no D2D copies, no dummy collectives, no extra NCCL launches, no added waits beyond the two synchronization points; all host work is O(1) per call.
setup_work.memory: No CUDA memory is allocated or retained by the candidate (no scratch tensors, no persistent buffers, no pools); setup and warm-run peak_allocated_bytes and reserved bytes are unchanged from baseline apart from transient host-side Python objects.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: Round state (open flag, staged element count, wrapper reference, flushed group work) resets at every round completion and on exception self-heals by deactivating; it is invariant across warmup, quality, repeats and profiling runs, never aliases model, optimizer or gradient state, and holds no fixture-dependent data. The returned Work objects are the parent op's own and follow the baseline lifecycle, including per-bucket future-result storage wiring.
setup_work.synchronization: All generated work is issued on the reducer's own call path and current stream inside the declared workload boundary. The only added synchronization is the per-enqueue and pre-launch current-stream host synchronize that orders the fused group launch after the final micro-batch's gradient writes; completion still flows through the reducer's existing per-bucket Work handling exactly as baseline. No barriers, no control-group collectives, no extra NCCL launches are introduced.

quality_risks: The central repair hypothesis is that the prior wte-region corruption was a read-before-write hazard of the deferred group launch; the added current-stream synchronizes make every gradient write GPU-complete before the parent op is enqueued and before _end_coalescing launches the group, which closes that hazard regardless of which internal ordering was deficient. If the corruption instead came from an unrelated grouped-launch defect, the paired project measurement would reproduce the deterministic wte signature and reject the candidate loudly rather than silently.

The reducer's Work contract was re-verified on CPU/gloo: Works must be the parent op's own (foreign pybind Works fail the c10d.Work capsule cast; tiny/dummy parent-op Works fail setStorage bounds because gradient storage is rewired onto the future result), and this candidate returns only parent-op Works for the caller's own bucket tensors, exactly as the mechanically-successful prior trial did.

Coalesced-group matching relies on both ranks opening the group at the round's first bucket and issuing identical collectives in identical order; baseline per-PG NCCL matching already requires the same bucket order, and discovery observed identical counts (12x 7,087,872-element plus 1x 39,385,344-element buckets) and shapes on both ranks, so a divergence would corrupt the baseline too.

NCCL may realize the coalesced group as one fused kernel or a small number of kernels whose bandwidth on the ~497.8MB aggregate over SHM is not guaranteed to reach the observed ~8.2GB/s; the worst case is approximately baseline kernel work plus ~1-3ms of host synchronization, with step_ms still bounded by the 1.05x cap (~161.5ms vs ~153.7ms baseline) and re-measured by the paired runs.

The added host synchronizes run on the reducer's call path inside the measured boundary; in this launch-bound eager workload each drain is expected to be near-zero because the GPU tracks the host's enqueue rate, but a systematically deep enqueue backlog could add up to the in-flight tail's execution time, which the step_ms constraint bounds.

DDP rebuilds buckets after early iterations; round completion is total-elements based (sum of model parameter numels), so any rebuilt layout that still partitions the same parameters closes its group exactly at round completion, and the overflow path (staged exceeding the total) flushes the pending group with all issued collectives intact and deactivates rather than mis-reducing. Bucket layouts with unchanged totals were exercised across repeated rounds in the CPU validation.

Capability fallback (signature mismatch, missing _start_coalescing/_end_coalescing, wrapper resolution failure, or any unexpected exception) permanently deactivates coalescing for the process and serves pure parent passthrough with both call sites still executing: exact baseline semantics, bitwise-equal gradients and valid coverage at baseline performance - validated bitwise on the CPU/gloo replica where gloo rejects _start_coalescing and the fallback reproduces baseline gradients across repeats.

No observations, thresholds, workload parameters, batch/sequence/accumulation semantics, dtype, RNG usage, data or completion boundaries are altered; the candidate does not read inputs or fixture outputs, holds no fixture-dependent state, and does not precompute any result.
